I've.

Don't know why.
Ah, there we go.
All right, Good stuff.
There you go.
Stayed in.
I'm doing well.
How are you?
Yeah.
Whereabouts you based?
I'm based.
I.
I live in Brooklyn.
I'm in Manhattan at the moment, so.
Cool.
Right.
We're based in London and New York and Los Angeles, but I'm in Somerset at the moment, which in the west of England, so.
Yeah, lovely.
My, My wife's from Wales.
So.
How is she?
Well, same, same size.
So she's just a bit further up the country.
Not too far.
Just down.
Down the M4.
Exactly.
Whereabouts in Wales is she from?
Just, Just over the seven bridge, so.
Oh, really?
Okay.
Yeah, not too far.
Yes, Past Bath.
Keep going, you'll get there.
Two hours from.
Oh, my God.
An American that knows where he is on the UK map.
Fantastic.
Yeah, a little bit, you know, spend a good amount of time in the uk.
We're the same county as Bath and it's about an hour away, so.
Yeah, yeah, brilliant.
Okay.
Well, nice to meet you and thank you for your time today.
Appreciate it's fairly speculative given the approach that we've made, but it's always good to understand other agencies, even if you're not ready to sell right now.
But a little bit about us.
We're a capital A group.
We are an M and a advisory for marketing services businesses.
So all of our clients either buy or sell side.
It always involves an agency of some sort, although we do work with private equity and private investors as well on the buy side.
And we have a platform, Agencies Co, which is our platform for agency owners to buy and sell businesses.
So great to meet you today.
Be really good to hear a little bit about EI Digital and where you're at.
I know you've kind of already said you're not really looking to sell, but you've had some offers in the past and you seem pretty up to speed in terms of the valuation of your own company.
It'd be good to know a little bit more and see if we've got any either buyers or sellers that can.
Can help you or whether we can actually find you some buyers yourself by listing on agencies.
Go.
Sure.
Yeah.
I mean, I don't think we're.
We.
We're interested in, you know, I guess that the flavor of a deal we'd be interested in would Be one that has you know, some sort of really good strategic fit.
So you know it would be either a group who we would fit in really well with and be part of a roll up with, you know, kind of two bites at the Apple type scenario.
Good match of culture, good match of what we do plugs in well, you know a creative sort of deal or something where there's a.

Not an agency deal but like a, you know, a company for example we do a lot in spirits, you could spirits holding company or something like that where it could be very, you know again a good strategic alignment there.
So something like that.
You know we're I think our differentiator if you were, would be that we're boutique but very integrated agencies.
So we are both understand the brand and the performance side and kind of build strategic plans that are what we call full funnel.
Right.

So we can think about great consumer experience and high touch kind of brand side but also operate CRM, email conversion media, things that are a little bit more measurable, optimizable from an analytical sense.
Work with a lot of spirits brands.
Latin Bev Alk we're rebranding, launching a private jet company that'll launch in April.
We have worked a lot in medical aesthetics and you know, med spa related industries.
Not too much actual proper pharma but you know, things that are technically pharma or regulated.

And then we've also worked in a lot of ad tech and other technical sort of industries service wise we've got you know, strategy and creative kind of at the heart of what we do and then delivery against digital marketing which includes, you know, paid media and CRM data, social content creation and technology with a dev team.
We build, manage mostly web platforms and related, you know, marketing platforms.
So that's us in a quick nutshell and again from any M and A.
We're not interested right now.

I don't think in you know, putting ourselves officially on the market necessarily but you know I'm, I'm always interested to see what's out there and, and like I said, we're interested in you know, accretive opportunities let's say.

So if there was a, something that was a really good fit could make a ton of sense, we could get a decent valuation and an opportunity to roll over equity into something bigger that could be interesting.
Right.
We, we would explore that kind of deal.
Okay, so whereabouts are you sort of in size of, in terms of your size today?
How many team members do you have?
About 30 people full time freelancers supplementing that.
So Working team might be 35 to 40 at any time and then distributed mostly in the US we're starting to explore more Latin America team members as well, which I'm excited about actually.
And then, you know, revenue wise, we'll hopefully do about 7 million this year.
And we aim to run, you know, roughly a 20% margin, give or take.
Against that we recently hired a head of operations, head of project management.
So we've made a lot of investment in kind of our infrastructure as a group, trying to get myself and my partner much more out of the day to day operational side and engage more.
So I have more opportunity to have meetings like this and do more biz, dev, et cetera.
Okay, do you know what your number was roughly for the last year as well, prior to the 7 million revenue?
We did, we did a gross 6.5 about last year.
Okay, so the business is growing, that's how.
And this year, are you, sorry, are you saying that the Last sort of training 12 months was 7 million or is that what you're projecting for this year?
That's what we're, we're targeting for this year.
I mean that would definitely require us to win projects and clients we don't have right now, but would expect that we will pick up business for actively pitching, have things in the pipeline, etc.
We probably have a, you know, booked about six or so.
Okay.
What do you guys look for?
I mean, what do you know, understanding.
It's sort of exploratory, but you know.
Yeah, that's, that's kind of our high level.
Yeah, so.
So we work on the buy and the sell side.
When we work on the buy side, what are we looking for?
It really depends on what the client, the client's brief is.
So they will give us a set of criteria and we're going out to look for exactly that in terms of sort of general rules of thumb around marketing agencies.
You know, we're usually looking for a company where there's a good layer of management team and usually a margin around 20% as well.
So I think in terms of everything that you're doing there, that's pretty much on the money.
That's kind of what a lot of good buyers are looking for.
And you'll get better multiples because of those things being in place.
So.
So that's definitely where it's at.
Yeah.
In terms of the market, it's very buoyant.
There's a lot of activity and we like, I say we won't both buy on the sell side.
So we've got probably two deals that are going to close this week and on the buy side we just closed a couple, both in the UK and the US For a UK comp.
A US company.
Sorry.
So bought one in the uk, one in the US So we've seen a ton of activity.
So yeah, I mean it depends what you're looking for really.
I just wonder.
Jesse, it's difficult to give you an answer like we have this deal here for you unless we've approached you directly for a client, then we wouldn't have anything that was definitely a fit.
But certainly we can keep you in mind for something.
But what I suggest possibly if, if you are interested in sort of a risk free approach would perhaps to.
To list on our platform agencies code and I know you said you don't really want to be out there but the things.
The entire process is anonymous and it's completely free to list as well.
So the idea really is you put the listing up, it has a teaser that explains the kind of business that you do.
You try not to put anything there.
Obviously it will give away who it is.
So yeah, I mean that's the, the key thing.
So you could say, you know, east coast based agency that focuses on spirits, brands or whatever and then we can put you out to our network.
We have 20,000 people subscribed to that and if you get a bite then you know there's interest out there and you can maybe invest more time and money into dealing with interest.
Right.
When you say time and money, does that mean to take the next step we would have to engage with you or what does that look like further?
Yeah, so no, you would be engaged with us already.
So once you list on the platform we'd have a engagement letter in place.
It's more about how much effort you want to put in to responding to that interest.
So we charge $5,000 to put together all the marketing, have a pitch deck, do the valuation, etc.
Etc.
You can either do it yourself or you can ask us to do it.
Those are the two flavors really.
But obviously we're working on your behalf.
As soon as we get that interest in.
And so our M and A team will be on all the calls, making sure we get a deal done, negotiated, et cetera, et cetera.
Until we close, we take 5% of the consideration as a win fee and that's how we work for probably about 50% of our clients.
We also.
It really does depend.
I mean you're saying it's not urgent so it wouldn't apply to you.
But some clients come to us and they say, you know, I want to sell, I want to it out.
And so that option costs.
Is that me or you?
Me.
So that option costs 24,000.
Sorry 30,000 actually in dollars.
Thinking in pounds.
And basically then we, we put together a whole plan and a strategy and we go out to market and we get that deal closed within six months.
So if you're not bothered about when that transaction happens, I suggest listing for free.
It's risk free.
If you want us to do a bit of work to get you ready, then it's $5,000.
It's not huge outlay and we'll get together all the marketing materials for you.
If you want to do it yourself then that's the options basically.
And you can test the market.
Sure.
I mean I would say why don't you send me an email with just like the net.
Net process and cost, things like that and I'll have a think about it.
You know, if it's truly you know, anonymous risk free retest, you know, might be interested in, in doing that.
You know again what, what I'd be interested in is if there was the right culturally aligned, you know again, you know, for example, do you have been.
You're in the uk do you know together group, you know those guys?
Yeah, they're based roll up.
Have they approached you?
Yeah, I spoke to them.
We were actually one of the.
Right.
When they did their first deal with Purple pr.
I spoke to the guys there and they had a really interesting model.
Right.
That it basically, you know, give you 30% down, 30% over two years and then 30% in equity and or 33% and you know, I thought that was kind of interesting.
They're basically rolling it all together.
We didn't do that deal but I liked how it was, you know the sort of general structure and I think we'd be again the type of thing we'd look.
We'd want to be able to take fair amount off the table but have reasonable upside in a vision towards a second deal.
Yeah.
So in terms of the anonymity of it.
So basically we put a listing up.
All we send out to get the interesting is what we call a teaser.
So that doesn't include any details of the company.
Once somebody's responded to that, they sign an NDA and then we field those NDAs to you.
So before we release any details in the next stage we make sure that you're okay with that.
If it's, you know, a rival or somebody that you've dealt with before that you wouldn't want to give details to, obviously you just refuse.
And then if it's somebody you don't mind, we release what's called an im.
And this is the piece that is going to cost time or money for somebody, but once they've got that im, then that's the full details on the deal and what the opportunity is.
And so that's the only point when it becomes an anonymous.
So there's no real way of anybody knowing for sure it's you.
Obviously if you're saying it's a, you know, a drinks agency or whatever, people might think there's only a few good ones that I can think of and they might guess you.
Yeah, sure.
In terms of the deal structure.
So it's very, very normal to have a deal structure.
Little like together, I would say they're pretty low on the cash offer but a bit higher on the equity.

So usually what we get is something akin to 40% of the cash or 40% of the value upfront then in earnouts over a three year period and like a 20% equity rollover which, which is the kind of standard is around 20, I would say 30 is a bit much, but they're obviously doing that because they're low on capital or whatever their original reason was for doing that.
Right, yeah, I'm sure it's changed over time.
I think it's still pretty similar the last time I talked to them, but they've been fairly successful and they're going after high end agencies as well.
But most deals out there are kind of that 40, 40, 20 structure.
The other half are just complete buyouts, but they would still structure 50% cash up front and 50% earn out something along those lines.
That's the pretty particular types of deals that you're going to see.
Yeah, that you're looking at.
That's kind of.
And what are you seeing in terms of multiple of EBITDA?
Yeah, well, the same as we discussed on LinkedIn.
So four to six, kind of the standard for agencies.

I would say most buyers are kind of looking in that window and most deals sort of end up somewhere in the middle of that, the upper end of that 5.5 or 6x and then beyond that when you get like certain variables that are going to push that up a little bit.
So it could be things like you've got amazing clients, it could be that you've got long contracts, it could be just in a sexy space.
So, you know, for spirits, for instance, there could be a really good strategic buyer that just wants to be buying your type of agency so that they may, they may push those multiples up.
So you might get.
So although there's kind of an industry average that ends up around there, you will get one or two points above that depending on the agency and also the quality of the work that you're doing, etc.
Etc.
So.
And also, like I mentioned before, you know, if you've got a, A management team in place, you know, if you, if you've got great margins, you know, there's all sorts of things that would push it up.
That makes sense.
Take a look at the books to sort of give you what we would say.
You know, we're confident in pitching you at this price.
That's part of the valuation process that we do and that's part of that 5k.

So to get you ready for market, to get you valued, to go through your books, you know, to really be able to dig down and tell you what your EBITDA probably is, because we can make some adjustments, give you evaluation, then create that marketing materials in response to those initial bits of interest that we get.
So, yeah, I mean, an email sent over and see how you do with that.
I can follow you in a couple of weeks to see where you're at.
Yeah, sounds good.
And either way, let's just, you know, we can stay in touch and see as things evolve, obviously as our, you know, EBITDA hopefully grows over time, then it.
Deals become more interesting.
Well, 20% is pretty good.
I would say it doesn't really need to grow.
A lot of buyers who, you know, the smart buyers are actually looking for that 20% because what it does.
No, sorry, not, not the percentage, but the total.
Right, right.
Just, you know, like if it's 20% of 10 million, it's.
Of course, if you do 400 million, then 20 is awesome.
Exactly.
You know.
Yeah.
Okay, well, 20 is a good margin.
So of course, yeah, if you, if you're doing 10 million next year, that's even better.
But what I would say, Jess, if I'm talking to you, that it's quite important to you that you get that cultural aspect.
Right.
And really I think this is where the opportunity is with something like agencies or any other M and a advisory you choose to go with that can put a process together for you.
Because what happens is people knock on your door and they're in charge of the driving seat, you know, they're probably speaking to or at least in contact 100 agencies, at least.
They may be speaking seriously to two or three at any given moment.
So they're really in the driving seat when it comes to getting a good deal for them.

But for you to get a good deal, the only way I can guarantee that you're going to get a good match and get good chemistry and good culture fit for your people is for you to be in the driver's seat, for you to have three or four serious contenders at the table, and for you to pick the one that is the best fit.
And the only way you can do that is to go to market and be for sale.
But it can all be completely anonymous.
There's no sign outside the door.
Nobody knows.
Your people shouldn't know either.
I mean, it's.
It's important.
Not even to let them.
Agreed.
Yeah.
Anyway, perfect.
Well, thanks.
Great to meet you, man.
Yeah, thanks so much.
Let's stay in touch.
Yeah.
Good to speak to you.
All right.
Have a great day.
Have you too.
Bye.

summary.overview: The Exploratory Business Discussion meeting between Jesse Resnick and Andy Day focused on the potential alignment between their companies, with Resnick representing EI Digital, a boutique integrated agency, and Day from Capital A Group, an M&A advisory firm. The meeting began with an overview of EI Digital's work with spirits brands, medical aesthetics, and ad tech, emphasizing their strategy and service offerings. It highlighted their financials, noting a goal of $7 million in revenue with a 20% profit margin for the year. The discussions evolved into an analysis of the current M&A landscape, characterized by active market conditions and typical deal structures for agencies, along with the importance of anonymity during the listing process. Action items included Resnick's consideration of listing EI Digital on the Agencies Co platform and Day's commitment to provide further details and follow up on the decision in the coming weeks.
summary.short_summary: Jesse Resnick from EI Digital and Andy Day from Capital A Group met to discuss potential collaboration between their companies. EI Digital, a boutique agency, specializes in brand and performance strategies for sectors like spirits, medical aesthetics, and ad tech, targeting $7 million in revenue with a 20% profit margin for the year. The conversation also delved into the current M&A landscape, revealing a buoyant market with typical deal structures involving 40% upfront payments, 40% earnouts, and 20% equity rollovers. EBITDA multiples for agencies range from 4 to 6, highlighting the active nature of the market. Action items included Resnick considering listing EI Digital on the Agencies Co platform, while Day committed to follow up with further details in the coming weeks.
